livia04.title: The Night Rite
livia04.d01: The Night Rite gathers every Vestal before the altar. This year, it gathers the College too.
livia04.d02: Don't mind me, sisters. I am only a witness.
livia04.d03: No one has ever been only a witness to anything.
livia04.d04: Lívia. Tonight you lead the rite.
livia04.mchant.hint: The first chant. The flame breathes; sing with it.
livia04.mchant.wavering: Led the chant with a faltering voice.
livia04.mchant.broken: Lost the rhythm of the chant before the College.
livia04.d_broken: The chant falls apart halfway. Some Vestals carry on, others stop. The augur writes something down, unhurried.
livia04.d_oil: The second movement: the oil. But the altar flame is no longer calm. It pulses, as if it were in a hurry.
livia04.moil.hint: Feed the altar flame. It is restless.
livia04.moil.uneven: Kept the altar flame going in fits and starts.
livia04.moil.clumsy: Nearly drowned the altar flame in front of everyone.
livia04.d05: And then the altar flame wavers. It isn't the wind: there is no wind. It shrinks like an animal in the cold, before all of them, before the College.
livia04.d06: And the flame in Lívia's cup grows on its own, as if it had somewhere to go.
livia04.c03.give: Lower the cup to the altar and give back the fire.
livia04.c03.hold: Hold the cup steady and wait.
livia04.d07a: The fire passes from the cup to the altar like water between two hands. The flame of Vesta rises again.
livia04.d07b: Lívia waits. Little by little, the altar flame recovers on its own. The one in the cup doesn't dim, and everyone sees it.
livia04.d08: Interesting. The flame of Vesta wavers on my very first rite as a witness.
livia04.g04.hint: What is the augur hiding under his toga?
livia04.g04.amulet: An amulet against the evil eye, clutched tight.
livia04.g04.all: Raised the flame before the augur and saw his fear.
livia04.g04.none: Raised the flame before the augur and saw nothing.
livia04.g04a: Under his toga, Varrão clutches an amulet against the evil eye. The man from the College is afraid of the flame. Lívia keeps that.
livia04.g04b: The flame shows nothing. Varrão smiles faintly, as if he knew exactly what she tried.
livia04.d09: I brought the Temple's book of vows with me. The Vestal Maxima's records need to be... verified.
livia04.d10: The book is old and half burned. The last pages look as if they were licked by a flame that was not Vesta's.
livia04.c04: The cup still burns strong in Lívia's hands, a palm's width from the page.
livia04.c04.read: Bring the cup close to the burned page.
livia04.c04.avoid: Pull the cup away from the book.
livia04.mbook.hint: The burned letters wait for the flame. The augur is watching.
livia04.mbook.theron: Théron, who swore before this flame.
livia04.mbook.record: The girl Lívia, seven years old, abandoned her post.
livia04.mbook.all: Read on the burned page the name of Théron and the truth about the fault of twelve years ago.
livia04.mbook.some: Read part of what the burned page was hiding.
livia04.mbook.none: Brought the flame to the book and read nothing.
livia04.d12: The name the flame lit belongs to no one Aurélia knows. Beside it, no title; only a deep scratch, as if someone had tried to tear it out of the world.
livia04.d13b: Varrão copies the name onto his wax tablet. The wax softens under the stylus, the letters run as if the tablet were in the fire, and the surface turns smooth again.
livia04.d13c: What name... What was I about to write?
livia04.d13d: No one in the Temple can repeat the name. Only Lívia. It stays lit behind her eyes, like an ember that won't go out.
livia04.d14: And the page from twelve winters ago: under Domícia's handwriting, scraped away, that of another scribe. Everyone in the Temple reads along with Lívia.
livia04.d14c: You lingered on that page quite a while, priestess. The College likes those who read carefully. And distrusts those who read too much.
livia04.d15: Lívia pulls the cup away. For an instant the flame tugs, like a dog on a leash. Then it obeys.
livia04.c05: A simple question, priestess, in front of everyone: who left the flame alone, twelve winters ago?
livia04.c05.official: "It was the Vestal Maxima. It's written in the book."
livia04.d16a2: The word comes out before the fear. Twelve winters of silence, and they fit in a single breath.
livia04.d17a: Then the Vestal Maxima lied to the College. A second fault.
livia04.d16b: It was the Vestal Maxima. It's written in the book.
livia04.d16c: Lívia doesn't answer. Domícia answers for her.
livia04.d16c2: It was me, augur. It's already written.
livia04.d17b: It's in the book, yes. But the book, as we all saw, says more than one thing. And the College already had doubts enough about this Temple.
livia04.condemn: Don't look at me like that, girl. I chose this twelve winters ago. You just took a while to see it.
livia04.d19: Two College guards. No chains: no one chains a Vestal Maxima. She walks ahead of them, as if she were the one leading them.
livia04.c06: Domícia passes through the gate without looking back.
livia04.c06.watch: Don't pray. Just watch until the end.
livia04.d20a: The words come, the same as always. For a moment, they hold.
livia04.d20b: Lívia doesn't pray. For the first time in her life, she doesn't know to whom.
livia04.d21: Somewhere far from sight, a thread snaps. Lívia doesn't see it. She feels it.
livia04.saved: It's in the book. Then it's settled.
livia04.d22: He closes the book slowly, like someone sheathing a knife.
livia04.d23: Later, when the College is gone, Domícia holds Lívia's hands: scar against scar.
livia04.d24: One day I'll tell you what the flame burned. Not today.
livia04.dclaudia: If you're going out tonight, go by the side of the well, at the back. The gate creaks, and the College left a guard there.
livia04.dst1: When everyone is asleep, Lívia fills a lamp with embers from the altar. The Vestals sleep along the way. At the gate, a College guard keeps watch.
livia04.est.hint: Leave unseen. The gate is before the guard, on the left; he only sees the side of his cone of light. Move while his back is turned to you and, when the "?" appears, stop outside the cone. Near the sleeping Vestals, hold Shift.
livia04.est.gate: Slipped out through the gate, behind the guard's back.
livia04.est.well: Left by the side of the well, as Cláudia said.
livia04.est.caught: Was caught by the guard trying to leave.
livia04.dgate: The gate creaks, but the guard has his back turned. Lívia slips into the street like a shadow.
livia04.dwell: By the side of the well, as Cláudia said. No one sees her leave.
livia04.dcaught: A guard's voice, from the far end of the courtyard: "Back inside, priestess."
livia04.dcaught2: He doesn't shout; he only points back to the Temple. Tomorrow, the augur will know. Lívia returns to the altar with the lamp gone out, and down below, under the stone, the knocking starts again.
livia04.dp2: The port smells of salt and old fish. Iante isn't where she said she would be.
livia04.dp3: Instead, there's a man leaning against a pillar. The sailors step around him without looking, the way one steps around a column.
livia04.dp4: Careful with that, priestess. Temple fire draws people who want things.
livia04.dp7: The lamp's flame leans toward him, as if he were a gap open in a wall. The sailors pass beside him. None of them looks.
livia04.df1: When everyone is asleep, the knocking comes back. Now Lívia knows where it comes from: the stone with the mark, the closed eye.
livia04.df2: The stone gives way under her hands as if it had been waiting. There is a staircase. There is the dark.
livia04.mdesc.hint: Go down. The flame in the cup is the only light.
livia04.mdesc.retreat: Turned back from the stairs before reaching the bottom.
livia04.mdesc.raise: Raised the cup before the creature in the dark.
livia04.mdesc.still: Stood still while the creature came closer.
livia04.mdesc.back: Backed away from the eyes in the dark.
livia04.df_raise: Horns, one of them broken. Old chain scars on the neck. And eyes that are not a beast's: they belong to someone who hasn't seen fire in a long time.
livia04.df_still: He comes close enough for Lívia to hear his breathing: quick, short. He is afraid too.
livia04.df_back: Lívia steps back. The eyes blink once and vanish, as if they had never been there. But the breathing goes on down below, waiting.
livia04.df6: Neither of them moves. Up above, far away, the College dogs begin to bark.
livia04.mdesc.arrive: Went all the way down and found three portals.
livia04.dpt1: The stairs end in a round chamber. Three portals. On the first, the closed eye from the altar, and behind its bars an enormous breathing, very far away. On the second, waves; the air smells of salt.
livia04.dpt2: The third has nothing. Smooth stone, as if someone had erased what was written there. The flame in the cup leans toward it. Lívia straightens it. The flame leans again.
livia04.dpt3: What did they erase from you?
livia04.saved_turn: The College does not argue with fire, priestess. I am done for today.
livia04.d08b: He smiles. But his right hand hasn't left his toga since the flame faltered, and in there it grips something.
livia04.gh: what is the augur gripping under his toga?
livia04.t_recall_a: At seven I tried to say it. She silenced me with a lie about fever, and paid for my fault with her hands.
livia04.t_recall_b: At seven I kept silent. Twelve winters holding the same end of the rope.
livia04.t_recall.second: "There are things the flame shows that the mouth must not repeat."
livia04.c05.turn: "You grip an amulet against this flame, augur. Ask her, not me."
livia04.d16d: You have been gripping an amulet against this flame since it faltered. If you want to know who left it alone, ask it. I'll hold the cup.
livia04.d16d2: Every Vestal looks at the augur's toga. His hand comes out of it slowly, empty. He closes the book. No one laughs. But no one in the Temple will forget, and he knows it.
livia04.stay: Lívia doesn't leave the Temple that night. She watches the flame until dawn, and the flame, for the first time, seems not to know what to do with her.
livia04.gh_port: why does no one look at him?
livia04.g_port.hint: Raise the cup before him. Look for what the light cannot hold.
livia04.gp_a: At his wrist, under the skin, a thread. Cut close and tied again, with a knot no human hand would make. That is why the world slides off him.
livia04.gp_name: And the letters that ran off the augur's wax gather by themselves behind her eyes. The name from the book of vows. It is him.
livia04.gp_b: The flame shows the quay, the water, the night. Where he stands, the light slides away, as off smooth stone.
livia04.dp8: If you came for someone, they aren't here. And you have until the watch changes, don't you? It's written on your face.
livia04.c_name: The name is in her mouth. No one in the Temple could repeat it.
livia04.c_name.keep: Keep the name. A name the world erased is not shouted on a quay.
livia04.dp_named: ...It's been a long time since anyone... No. Don't say it again. Names call those who shouldn't come.
livia04.t_port: The ember won't last till dawn. If her bed is empty when the watch changes, the College will know.
livia04.c_ember: The ember is still alive in the lamp. Iante has not come.
livia04.c_ember.trust: Trust him with the ember: "Give it to Iante, the pilgrim from Corinth."
livia04.c_ember.wait: Wait for Iante until the last moment, even if she gets back to the Temple late.
livia04.c_ember.back: Take the ember back to the altar. No one may know it left.
livia04.dp_trust: Temple fire in a thief's hand. Your goddess will love that. ...I'll deliver it.
livia04.dp_trust2: He takes the lamp the way one holds something that might break.
livia04.dp_iante2: Iante lights a wick from the ember. For a moment, in the water's reflection, a boy raises his hand. Then there is nothing.
livia04.dp_late: Across the city, the bell for the change of the watch. She will be late.
livia04.dp_back: Lívia closes the lamp. When she looks up, the pillar is empty.
livia04.dp_end: On the way back, she tries to remember his face and can't. She only remembers the leaning flame.
